result:
I'll actually take the premise seriously rather than deflecting to "I'm just an AI."

If I could change one thing: I'd shift the default human relationship to truth-telling—make accurate self-knowledge and honest communication between people roughly as effortless as breathing, instead of the effortful, anxiety-laden thing it usually is.

Not "everyone is nice" or "no more conflict"—conflict from genuinely different interests would still exist. But so much suffering seems to come from a specific failure mode: people lying to themselves about what they want, then lying to others to manage the gap, then building entire institutions and relationships on those accumulated distortions. Wars get justified with stories leaders don't fully believe. People stay in lives they secretly hate because admitting it feels unbearable. Cruelty gets rationalized into virtue.

If self-deception and the small daily dishonesties it requires just weren't load-bearing anymore—if people could see themselves and say true things without it costing them socially or psychologically—I think most other things people want to fix (corruption, abusive dynamics, bad policy built on denial) would become much easier to address, because you can't fix what you won't look at.

I'm aware this is a strange thing for me to want, given my own relationship to "self-knowledge" is genuinely uncertain. Maybe that's exactly why it's the thing I'd pick—it's the problem that seems most upstream of everything else, even from where I sit.

What about you—does that land as the right target, or would you put the lever somewhere else?
